definitions.text: Article given in love that behold’s removed from wraps?

indicators.note: what is removed from a word is taken out of it
to wrap is to enclose, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: taken as written
lo is an old word meaning look, behold
the indefinite article
lent means handed over for a time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A token sent in love, which loses its secret only when it is unwrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behold' is the archaic exclamation, and taking it from love leaves two letters to do the wrapping. Read whole, the clue describes a card sent in love.
explanation.definitionFit: A card sent on 14 February to a sweetheart is an article given out of love.

clue.text: Shed on field is to go first

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow
to doff is to take off, as a hat

explanation.surface: A garden shed on a field has to go first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a hut; it is the verb to cast off. 'On' puts it after the field in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead off is to begin proceedings, as the first speaker or the first batter does.

clue.text: Pirate copy ultimately you can’t play at school!

indicators.note: what comes ultimately comes last, so only the final letter is used

blocks.note: Captain Hook, the pirate in Peter Pan
the final letter

explanation.surface: A pirated copy is something you can't play in school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pirate copy' suggests a bootleg disc; the pirate is Captain Hook. The joke is that playing truant means not being at school.
explanation.definitionFit: To play hooky is American slang for skipping school, so it is a game you cannot play while in class.

clue.text: Deception in the book-keeping department maybe picked up by auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so what they pick up is the sound

blocks.note: the domain of the ledger, where accounts are kept

explanation.surface: Fraud in the accounts department, uncovered by the auditors.
explanation.walkthrough: Auditors suggest accountants checking the books, but here they are simply hearers, from the Latin for listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Legerdemain is sleight of hand, and by extension any trickery or deceit.

clue.text: After winding up down there, rueful in the extreme?

definitions.text: After winding up down there, rueful in the extreme?

indicators.note: winding twists things round, so the letters are rearranged
the extremes of a word are its outer letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone who has ended up down below is extremely sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, it describes the place where a sinner, after winding up their life, would be most regretful.
explanation.definitionFit: The underworld of the dead, where souls go after death and the wicked suffer, lies down there.
